newsitem.title: FINLAND: INSTANT VIEW - Nokia Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Nokia Q1 results.

text.p: Following are some first responses from analysts to Nokia's first-quarter report:
"The cashflow was positive which was good. With Ericsson people took it negatively because it had negative cashflow. But Nokia's was positive."
"From our perspective the revenue growth was excellent, the gross margin was excellent, they've got inventories under control and we're very pleased."

He mentioned a comparison of overall mobile handsets and systems sales growth between Nokia, Ericsson and Motorola. Nokia put in 48 percent, Ericsson 42 percent, Motorola four percent -- but Nokia had a very weak Q1 last year.
"We have a 1:1 recommendation for Nokia and a 2:1 for Ericsson and Motorola, on valuation grounds." (1:1 is more bullish than 2:1).
Too early in the year to look at full-year forecasts.
"On the face of it this looks very good. Particularly that they managed to be cash-positive."
"I think I will (upgrade my forecast) but probably not dramatically."
Has a "hold" recommendation for the stock, plans to maintain this; further stock gains depend on U.S. investors' reaction.
At conference call due 1500/1200 GMT, expects main question in mobile phones to focus on operating margin: "Is it over 10 percent?" @
Another question would be on any currency effects in overall result, and their impact.
"The result looked good. Growth was as expected. Like with Ericsson, the growth on the mobile phones side was staggering."
"The research projects in Japan are positive. It's good to be visible in Japan."
